source_basis: Public ISO catalogue pages, official standard scope summaries and ISA/IEC 62443 series overview checked on 2026-11-15. This is an applicability triage aid, not the normative standard text. Full standards, national adoptions, regulatory instruments and the actual machine/task/site documentation must be reviewed by competent safety and legal professionals.

machine_classes.description: A fixed industrial robot with end-effector, workpiece, supporting machinery and a defined industrial application/cell.
standard_hypotheses: ISA/IEC 62443 series where connected IACS assets exist
mandatory_review_questions: Is the robot within the industrial-robot scope and intended workplace conditions?
Are all application hazards from tooling, workpiece, process, structures and adjacent machines assessed?
Which safety functions are required and who owns their design and validation?
Does public or non-working-adult access change the applicable framework?
Which cybersecurity controls apply to the robot, controller, engineering workstation and site network?

machine_classes.description: A robot manipulator mounted on a mobile platform, driverless industrial truck, AGV or autonomous mobile robot.
standard_hypotheses: ISO 3691-4:2023 where the base vehicle falls within driverless industrial-truck definitions
ISO 10218-1:2025 and ISO 10218-2:2025 only for robot/application elements within their scope; do not assume they cover the mobile base or combined system
ISA/IEC 62443 series where connected IACS assets exist
mandatory_review_questions: Does the mobile base qualify as a driverless industrial truck under the applicable definitions?
Are combined manipulator, payload, mobile base, navigation and site hazards assessed as one application?
Is the operating zone prepared and controlled for the task?
Does operation in public zones, public roads, explosive atmospheres or severe conditions trigger exclusions or other standards?
Are localization, navigation, protective sensing, braking and emergency functions independently specified and validated?

machine_classes.description: Autonomous or semi-autonomous earth-moving machinery or mobile mining machines operating on surface or underground work sites.
standard_hypotheses: ISO 17757:2019 where the machine and autonomous/semi-autonomous system fit its definitions
ISO 13849-1:2023 or other applicable functional-safety standards as determined by the safety architecture
Machine-specific earth-moving/mining machinery standards for baseline machine hazards
ISA/IEC 62443 series where connected IACS assets exist
mandatory_review_questions: Does the machine fall within ISO 6165 earth-moving machinery definitions or the mobile-mining-machine scope?
Is the autonomy system boundary defined across machines, infrastructure, communications and software?
Are surface/underground conditions and interaction with manually operated equipment included?
Are remote-control functions separately assessed where applicable?
What machine-specific standards and jurisdictional mining/construction regulations supplement ISO 17757?

machine_classes.description: Cranes, lifting devices, forklifts or other plant whose primary function is lifting/transporting material.
standard_hypotheses: ISO 10218-2:2025 is not a universal coverage route for multi-purpose lifting devices or machinery such as cranes and forklift trucks
Machine-specific lifting, crane, hoist, forklift and local statutory requirements; exact standard set NOT_ASSESSED in this profile
mandatory_review_questions: What is the equipment classification and rated lifting function?
Which machine-specific lifting/hoisting standards and statutory requirements govern?
Are suspended-load dynamics, rigging, load path, ground bearing, wind and exclusion zones addressed?
Who is the competent person responsible for lift planning and authorization?
Are robotic positioning functions separate from load-handling safety functions?

machine_classes.description: A specialist robot operating underground (for example inspection, drilling, lining, material handling or tunnel works) that may not be earth-moving machinery or a mobile mining machine.
standard_hypotheses: ISO 17757:2019 only where the system fits its earth-moving/mobile-mining machine definitions; do not extend its scope automatically to every underground robot
Applicable machine/product standards and national mining, tunnel and construction regulations require expert identification
ISA/IEC 62443 series where connected IACS assets exist
mandatory_review_questions: Is the machine an earth-moving machine or mobile mining machine within ISO 17757 scope?
What underground-specific hazards exist (ventilation, atmosphere, fire, egress, ground control, water, communications and rescue)?
Which local mine/tunnel and construction regulations govern the actual site?
Are loss-of-comms, localization degradation and evacuation/recovery states independently validated?
Does the public industrial-robot standard exclude the deployment environment or platform mobility?

standards.title: Robotics — Safety requirements — Part 1: Industrial robots
standards.scope_summary: Safety requirements for industrial robots as machines/partly completed machinery, including inherent design and information for integration.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: The published scope excludes underground use.
It excludes mobility when robots or manipulators are fixed to or part of driverless industrial trucks or mobile platforms.
It addresses the robot itself; application and robot-cell integration are addressed in Part 2.
Public access and non-working-adult contexts are outside the stated industrial workplace scope.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Record robot identity, model and configuration digests, operating modes, tool/payload identities and integration boundaries.
Retain design and test evidence references, but do not infer conformity from these records.
standards.non_claim: A motion oracle, collision check or envelope receipt does not establish ISO 10218-1 conformity or validate safety functions.

standards.title: Robotics — Safety requirements — Part 2: Industrial robot applications and robot cells
standards.scope_summary: Safety requirements for the design, integration, commissioning, operation, maintenance, decommissioning and disposal of industrial robot applications and cells.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: The published scope excludes multi-purpose lifting devices or machinery, including cranes and forklift trucks.
It is not a universal standard for mobile platforms, underground specialist robots or all construction plant.
The application includes workpieces, task programs and supporting machinery; the robot alone is not the complete safety case.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Record application identity, workpiece/task program, machine interfaces, lifecycle state, design revision and commissioning/maintenance/inspection evidence.
Bind acceptance records to the exact configuration and operating context.
standards.non_claim: An application record or digital-twin model cannot certify the integrated robot application or replace integrator responsibilities.

standards.title: Earth-moving machinery and mining — Autonomous and semi-autonomous machine system safety
standards.scope_summary: Safety requirements for autonomous/semi-autonomous earth-moving and mobile mining machines and their associated systems/infrastructure, hardware and software, including surface and underground applications.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: Applicability depends on the machine fitting the referenced earth-moving machinery or mobile-mining-machine definitions.
Remote-control capability is addressed separately (ISO 15817).
Function-specific automated features are outside the scope unless used as part of the autonomous/semi-autonomous machine system.
It is not automatically applicable to every underground inspection, construction or service robot.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Record machine/system boundary, infrastructure dependencies, operating environment, surface/underground mode, communication state, configuration and lifecycle evidence.
Bind machine/system evidence to exact site epoch, work package, design and controller versions.
standards.non_claim: An occupancy map or collision result does not satisfy ISO 17757 requirements or establish autonomous machine-system safety.

standards.title: Industrial trucks — Safety requirements and verification — Part 4: Driverless industrial trucks and their systems
standards.scope_summary: Safety requirements and verification for driverless industrial trucks and their systems; examples include AGVs, autonomous mobile robots, bots and automated guided carts.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: The operating zone has significant effect on safe operation; operating-zone preparation is addressed in the standard.
The 2023 edition excludes public zones and public-road operation, among other listed special environments and hazards.
The third edition is under development; draft text is not treated as a published requirement in this profile.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Record vehicle class, safety sensors, operating-zone survey/revision, navigation configuration, speed/braking modes, load/payload and validation results.
Bind route/occupancy observations to the exact operating zone and site state.
standards.non_claim: An AMR-style navigation stack or occupancy reservation is not proof of ISO 3691-4 conformity or operating-zone safety.

standards.title: Safety of machinery — General principles for design — Risk assessment and risk reduction
standards.edition_or_series: ISO 12100:2010, Edition 1; reviewed and confirmed in 2022
standards.scope_summary: General machinery safety terminology, principles and methodology for hazard identification, risk assessment and risk reduction across relevant lifecycle phases, including documentation and verification.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: This is a general methodology; relevant type-B and type-C standards and jurisdictional laws may impose more specific requirements.
The next revision ISO/DIS 12100.3 is under development; use the published edition unless a competent standards authority directs otherwise.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Provide traceable hazard, assumption, risk-control, verification, residual-risk and change records.
Keep unknown or unverified hazards explicit; preserve links between design revision, controls and validation evidence.
standards.non_claim: The platform can store risk-assessment evidence but cannot perform or approve a complete risk assessment by itself.

standards.title: Safety of machinery — Safety-related parts of control systems — Part 1: General principles for design
standards.scope_summary: Methodology and requirements/guidance for design and integration of safety-related parts of control systems, including software, for high-demand and continuous modes.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: It is a safety-control-system design methodology, not a standalone robot or application standard.
Required performance levels, architecture, component data, validation and lifecycle responsibilities must be determined by the safety engineering process.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Record safety-function identifiers, requirement revisions, component/software configuration, diagnostic/test evidence and independent validation receipts.
Preserve failure and unresolved states; do not infer a required performance level from nominal controller behavior.
standards.non_claim: A software unit test or successful CI job is not a PL claim, functional-safety validation or proof of a safety function.

standards.title: Security for industrial automation and control systems
standards.edition_or_series: ISA/IEC 62443 series; edition varies by part
standards.scope_summary: Cybersecurity standards and processes for industrial automation and control systems, addressing OT security across asset owners, integrators, suppliers and system components.
scope_exclusions_or_limits: This is a cybersecurity series, not a machinery safety standard.
Select the applicable parts and editions for the actual asset, system, service-provider and lifecycle boundary.
Cybersecurity controls do not replace functional safety or physical risk reduction.
symtropy_evidence_relationship: Record software/build digests, identities, access grants, change approvals, provenance, vulnerability disposition and event/audit receipts.
Bind security posture records to the exact deployed controller, network zone and release.
standards.non_claim: An audit log, signed build or evidence receipt alone does not demonstrate an IEC 62443 security level or certification.

revision_watch.status: Third edition under development; do not substitute draft requirements for ISO 3691-4:2023 in a conformity claim.
revision_watch.handling: Track the published status and national adoption before updating the applicable edition.
Keep the published edition and draft revision separate in all applicability records.

revision_watch.status: Published 2025 editions replacing the withdrawn 2011 editions.
revision_watch.handling: Use the exact 2025 part and edition; do not carry forward assumptions from 2011 without reviewing revised scope and requirements.

prohibited_inferences: A passing geometry test does not prove collision freedom on a physical robot.
A passing CI run does not establish functional safety, a performance level, a safety integrity level or regulatory conformity.
An ISO number appearing in a project manifest does not mean the standard applies or that the application conforms.
A public scope summary is not a substitute for the complete normative standard text.
ISO 10218 does not universally cover mobile platforms, underground operation, cranes, forklifts or every construction robot.
ISO 17757 is not automatically applicable to every underground robot; machine definitions and operational scope must match.
A standard applicability status is not a permission to operate or an independent safety acceptance.
